core_obligations: Write det_kappa(u_M) = f_M times the identity and observe that the three maps u_K, u_L, u_M form an isomorphism of the short exact sequence 0 -> K -> L -> M -> 0 (proof lines 16522-16526).
Apply the equivariance part of the determinant additivity lemma to that isomorphism of short exact sequences to obtain the multiplicative relation f_K f_M = f_L (proof lines 16527-16528).
Conclude by induction on the length that f_M = u-bar^l, since the relation makes f additive over short exact sequences and the length one case is immediate (proof lines 16529-16530).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a multiplicativity relation for the scalars f_M through an isomorphism of short exact sequences (proof lines 16522-16528).
Conclude by induction on the length from the length one case (proof lines 16529-16530).
difficulty_reason: The lemma determines the action of multiplication by a unit u of a local ring on the determinant of a finite length module M: it is multiplication by the image of u raised to the l-th power, where l = length_R(M) (statement lines 16504-16519). The proof is an induction on the length organised through the additivity of the determinant functor: writing det_kappa(u_M) = f_M id, the author takes a short exact sequence 0 -> K -> L -> M -> 0 of finite modules, observes that u_K, u_L, u_M form an isomorphism of short exact sequences, and applies the equivariance property of the determinant isomorphism to get the multiplicativity relation f_K f_M = f_L (proof lines 16522-16528). This makes f_M multiplicative in the length and reduces the claim to modules of length one, where it is trivial (proof lines 16529-16530). Recognising that the equivariance property of the determinant isomorphism is exactly the multiplicativity needed for the induction is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
